title: 2021 Filippi F1 Single Scull
highlights: One owner from new
Carbon wing rigger with quick-set spread
Hull weighed and certified at 14.0 kg
description: Bought new by the club in 2021 for our lightweight squad and used for four seasons on the Rotsee. Stored indoors in slings its whole life, never trailered abroad. The hull is straight with no repairs; there is light gelcoat crazing at the bow ball and a scuff on the port gunwale from a landing stage. Sold with the original Filippi shoes (size 44), bow ball, and a fitted top cover. Riggers and seat included, sculls are not.
photoDirection: Three-quarter bow view on a still lake at dawn, hull half in shadow, Rotsee-style tree line behind. Close-up of the wing rigger casting and of the bow number holder.

title: 2026 Empacher Single Scull — Built to Order
highlights: Built to your weight and rig preferences
10–14 week lead time from order
Two-year hull warranty
description: New-build slot for the 2026/27 season. Specify your crew weight band, shoe size, rigger height and preferred spread at order and the boat is laid up accordingly. Price is for the standard honeycomb layup in the classic yellow deck; custom paint and the lightweight layup are quoted separately. Delivery across the EU, or collect from Dortmund. Sculls, cover and boat stands available as a package.
photoDirection: Workshop shot: bare hull on trestles under overhead lighting, yellow deck catching the light. Detail of the Empacher rigger stamp and the hull weight plate.

title: 2019 Hudson S4X Single Scull
highlights: Raced masters only — never a college boat
Professionally repaired stern section (2023, documented)
Includes Hudson shoes and top cover
description: My training single for six seasons on Lake Washington. Honest condition: it has been raced and it looks it. There is a repaired stern puncture from a dock collision in 2023 — done properly by a composite shop in Portland, invoice included, and it has not moved since. Deck hardware is all present and the tracks are clean. Selling because I have moved into a double with my training partner.
photoDirection: Boat on club slings against a grey Pacific Northwest sky, water flat behind. Honest close-up of the repaired stern section, plus the tracks and footstretcher.

title: 2016 Peinert Zephyr Single Scull
highlights: Stable enough to learn in, quick enough to race masters
Wide weight band — suits a shared or club boat
Freshly serviced tracks and wheels
description: The Zephyr is the boat we put every new sculler into, and this one has done that job for ten years. It is forgiving at the catch and very hard to fall out of, which is exactly what you want in a first single. Cosmetically tired — scratches along both gunwales, faded decals — but structurally sound with no soft spots. New tracks and seat wheels fitted this spring. Ideal first boat or club spare.
photoDirection: Boat being carried down a dock by one rower, Boston skyline soft behind. Detail of the conventional rigger and the well-worn but clean tracks.

title: 2026 WinTech Club Trainer Single
highlights: In stock — no lead time
Built for learn-to-row and rough water
Fleet pricing on three or more
description: The workhorse club single. Glass hull, wide waterline, and a weight band broad enough that the whole learn-to-row cohort can use the same boat. Not a race hull and not pretending to be one — it is stable, cheap to repair, and survives being dropped on a dock. Two in stock in white, more available on a four-week build. Fleet discount applies from three boats.
photoDirection: Row of identical new club singles racked outside a boathouse, morning light raking across the hulls. Wide shot of a learn-to-row session on flat water.

title: 2014 Van Dusen Advantage Single
highlights: Cheapest race-legal carbon single currently listed
Needs cosmetic work — priced accordingly
Riggers and shoes included, no sculls
description: Sold as-is. This was a Schuylkill club boat before I bought it in 2020 and it has the dings to prove it: several stress cracks in the deck paint, a soft patch of gelcoat near the bow, and one rigger stay that has been straightened. It rows fine and I have used it three times a week, but a buyer should expect to spend a weekend and a few hundred dollars tidying it. Priced for someone who wants a light hull and does not mind a project.
photoDirection: Boat on grass beside the Schuylkill, Boathouse Row in the far background. Unflinching detail shots of the deck cracks and the straightened stay — honesty is the selling point.

title: 2018 Fluidesign Double Scull
highlights: Factory-serviced in 2025
Rigged for heavyweight women or lightweight men
Ships anywhere in North America
description: Retired from our senior squad after the 2025 season. Went back to Fluidesign for a full service last spring — new tracks, new wheels, hull inspected and cleared. No repairs, no soft spots. Comes with both sets of riggers, four shoes, bow ball and a full cover. We are replacing it with a new quad, not because there is anything wrong with this boat.
photoDirection: Two scullers lifting the double out of the water at a Canadian club dock, autumn colour on the far bank. Detail of the seat deck and the factory service sticker.

title: 2026 Filippi F14 Double Scull — New
highlights: Direct from the factory
Choice of layup and rigger geometry
Worldwide shipping quoted at order
description: Current-generation F14 hull, the double most seen at international regattas. Ordered direct: you choose layup, rigger geometry, footstretcher type and paint at the point of order, and the boat is built to that spec. Standard lead time is twelve weeks; a small number of build slots remain for delivery before the 2027 European season. Price shown is ex-works for the standard racing layup.
photoDirection: Factory floor: hull in the mould shop, Tuscan light through high windows. On-water shot of a double at speed, bow wave crisp, blades feathering.

title: 2015 Sykes Gold Medal Double Scull
highlights: Suits a lighter crew or a women's pairing
Bow section repaired 2021, professionally
Trailer-ready, straps included
description: Good honest masters double. It has been up and down the Hume for a decade of regattas, so the paint tells a story, but the hull is fair and it runs straight. Bow section was repaired after a launching mishap in 2021 by a Melbourne composite shop; the repair is visible under the paint and has never given trouble. Selling as the squad has aged out of the weight band.
photoDirection: Double on the Yarra at first light, city towers reflected. Wide shot of it strapped to a club trailer. Detail of the aluminium wing and the repaired bow.

title: 2012 Empacher Double Scull
highlights: Heavyweight layup — genuinely built for big crews
Deposit taken, viewing still welcome
Full set of spare riggers included
description: Classic Empacher club double in the heavier layup, which is why it is still going strong at fourteen years old. My partner and I have rowed it on the Amstel since 2019. The yellow has faded on the deck and there are the usual scuffs at the bow and stern, but nothing structural. A deposit has been taken subject to a viewing — if that falls through you are next in line, so do get in touch.
photoDirection: Boat on the Amstel with the low Dutch horizon and a windmill silhouette. Detail of the faded yellow deck showing honest age. Spare riggers laid out on a boathouse floor.

title: 2020 Hudson Ultimate Quad
highlights: Six seasons, one squad, indoor storage throughout
Converts to a coxed quad with the included stern seat
No repairs — hull has never been holed
description: Our top quad since 2020, retired only because we have taken delivery of a new one. Flat-water club in a warm climate, so no freeze damage and no winter storage problems. Rows with four sets of wing riggers, all included, plus the stern coxing seat and rudder linkage if you want to run it as a 4x+. Tracks and wheels replaced last winter. We will help load onto a trailer.
photoDirection: Quad on the water at Lady Bird Lake, downtown Austin skyline compressed behind it. Boathouse interior with the boat racked. Detail of the coxing seat conversion.

title: 2011 Vespoli Lightweight Coxed Four
highlights: Ideal junior or lightweight programme boat
Bow-loader with a working cox box mount
Priced to move before the autumn season
description: Fifteen years of junior rowing. It has been raced hard and repaired more than once — two patched sections on the bottom, both watertight, both documented in our maintenance log which we will hand over. The lightweight layup means it suits a junior girls' or lightweight men's crew rather than heavyweights. Everything works; nothing is pretty. If you run a programme on a budget this is a lot of boat for the money.
photoDirection: Junior crew shouldering the four up a ramp, coach launch in the background. Interior shot of the bow-loader cox position. Honest photos of both hull patches.

title: 2026 Filippi F4 Coxless Four — New
highlights: Built to order for a specific crew weight
Bow-steer or shoe-steer rudder
Factory support and spares for the life of the hull
description: The F4 in current specification, built to your crew's weight and rigging preference. Choose bow-steer or shoe-steer, footstretcher type, rigger geometry and paint at the point of order. Twelve-week lead time. Filippi supports the hull with spares indefinitely, which matters more than it sounds when you are trying to source a rigger part for a boat that is a decade old.
photoDirection: Four at racing pace from a coach launch, four blades locked in at the catch. Factory detail: a rigger being torqued onto a fresh hull.

title: 2017 Resolute Eight
highlights: Top-boat condition — genuinely excellent for its age
Full set of wing riggers plus a complete spare set
Boat, riggers and slings sold together
description: Our first eight from 2017 through the 2024 season, then second eight for one year. Stored indoors, covered, and washed after every salt or brackish outing. No holes, no patches, no soft spots — we have the annual inspection records. Comes with the complete wing rigger set, a full spare set, eight seats, bow ball, cox box mount, and four sets of slings. Buyer arranges transport; we will load.
photoDirection: Eight at full pressure, cox visible, water breaking cleanly off the bow. Boathouse shot of it racked at head height. Detail of the wing rigger and bowball.

title: 2008 Vespoli Eight — Club Boat
highlights: An entire eight for less than a good single
Rows every day — it is not a wreck, it is old
Ideal for a startup programme or a novice fleet
description: Eighteen years old and still on the water five days a week. This is a novice and masters boat, not a race boat: heavier layup, conventional riggers, forgiving to row. Expect cosmetic damage everywhere and three repaired sections along the bottom. What you are buying is a functional eight at a price that lets a new programme exist at all. We are only selling because a donor bought us a replacement.
photoDirection: Novice crew launching from a municipal dock, city behind. Wide shot of the whole hull on slings showing its honest, weathered state. Close-up of a repaired panel.

title: 2026 Empacher Eight — Built to Order
highlights: Indicative price — final quote depends on layup and paint
Build slots for the 2027 season
Delivery and rigging setup included within the EU
description: New-build eight in the racing layup. The figure shown is indicative for a standard specification; the final quote depends on layup, rigger choice, paint and delivery. Build slots remain for delivery ahead of the 2027 season. Within the EU we deliver the boat, rig it with your crew present, and take the trailer away — which is worth more than it sounds when the boat is eighteen metres long.
photoDirection: New eight being unloaded from a delivery trailer outside a boathouse, protective covers half off. Factory shot of the deck lamination. Yellow deck detail.

title: 2019 Swift Racing Coxless Quad
highlights: Raced at Henley Women's Regatta three years running
Serviced annually, records available
Viewing welcome on any weekday evening
description: Our senior women's quad from 2019 to 2025. Kept inside, covered, and serviced every winter by a Thames Valley boat repairer — we have the invoices. Two small stress cracks in the deck paint at the bow rigger, inspected and confirmed cosmetic. Full set of riggers, eight shoes across two sizes, bow ball and covers included. Happy to hold it for a week for a genuine buyer arranging transport.
photoDirection: Quad on the Henley reach, Temple Island in soft focus. Boathouse racking shot. Detail of the bow rigger and the cosmetic deck crazing.

title: 2013 Janoušek Coxless Pair
highlights: The cheapest way into pair rowing
Straight hull, no repairs
Bow-steer rudder fitted
description: Bought from a Midlands club in 2021 and rowed at the National Water Sports Centre ever since. Hull is straight and unrepaired; the paint is chalky on the sun-facing side from years on outdoor racking, which is honest wear and not structural. Bow-steer rudder is fitted and works. Includes both sets of riggers and four shoes. Selling because my pairs partner has moved abroad.
photoDirection: Pair on the flat water of a rowing course, marker buoys receding. Detail of the bow-steer linkage and of the chalky sun-faded paint.

title: 2026 LiteBoat LiteSport 1x — Coastal
highlights: Self-bailing — built for open water and chop
Almost impossible to swamp
In stock, two colours
description: Coastal rowing is the fastest-growing part of the sport and this is the boat most people start in. Self-bailing hull, wide beam, and enough reserve buoyancy that you can row it in conditions that would end a flat-water single. It is heavy and it is slow next to a racing scull — that is the trade for being able to launch off a beach into a metre of swell. Two in stock now.
photoDirection: Coastal single launching off a shingle beach through small surf, Alpine lake or Mediterranean coastline behind. Detail of the self-bailing ports and the reinforced bow.

title: 2021 Salani Coastal Single
highlights: Raced two coastal championships
Carbon layup — light for a coastal hull
Beach trolley and cover included
description: Raced at the Italian coastal championships in 2022 and 2023, then used for training out of Genoa. Salt water throughout its life, so the hardware shows corrosion and two rigger bolts have been replaced. Hull itself is sound with a scrape along the keel line from beach launches, which every coastal boat has. Includes the beach trolley, a cover, and a set of coastal blades if you want them for another €300.
photoDirection: Boat on a beach trolley on Ligurian shingle, Mediterranean behind. Keel-line scrape shot honestly. Corroded-but-serviceable rigger hardware close up.

title: 2022 Virus Boats Ares Coastal Double
highlights: Coastal endurance boat — built for distance, not sprints
Rinsed after every salt outing since new
Two sets of coastal sculls available separately
description: Bought new in 2022 for our coastal endurance group and looked after properly: freshwater rinse after every outing, stored under cover, hardware serviced each spring. It has done the Marseille–Cassis crossing four times. Genuinely excellent condition for a salt-water boat. Selling as the group has grown and we need a quad instead.
photoDirection: Coastal double at sea in a moderate swell, calanques cliffs behind. Detail of the salt-clean hardware. Boat on the beach at the end of a long row, crew stretching.

title: 2019 WinTech Coastal Single
highlights: Cheapest coastal boat on the site
Glass hull — easy and cheap to repair
Good introduction to open-water rowing
description: Club coastal boat since 2019, used for open-water sessions in Sarasota Bay. Glass hull means it is heavy but it also means a ding costs fifty dollars rather than five hundred. Expect scratches and sun-faded decals. Everything functional, self-bailers clear, seat and tracks recently cleaned. A sensible first coastal boat.
photoDirection: Boat pulled up on a white-sand Gulf beach at golden hour. Detail of sun-faded decals and the self-bailer. Rower launching through low surf.

title: 2019 Peinert 26 Recreational Single
highlights: Handles wind and boat wash better than a racing single
Light enough for one person to carry
Ideal masters or recreational boat
description: The boat I recommend to everyone who wants to scull for enjoyment rather than to race. Wider and shorter than a racing single, so it deals with chop, ferry wash and wind without drama, but it is still quick enough to be satisfying. Kept in a garage, rowed on Casco Bay three times a week for seven years. Immaculate apart from a small scuff at the stern. Includes cover and boat stands.
photoDirection: Sculler on calm coastal water at dawn, Maine islands and a lobster boat in the middle distance. Detail of the wider hull section. Boat on stands in a home garage.

title: 2016 Hudson Predator Coxless Pair
highlights: Sold July 2026 — kept listed for price reference
Wing-rigged pair with shoe steering
Sold to a club in Portland
description: This boat has sold. We leave sold listings up for six months so buyers and sellers can see what boats actually trade for, rather than what people ask. It was our senior men's pair from 2016 to 2025, wing-rigged with shoe steering, one repaired section at the stern, and it went to a club in Portland at the full asking price within twelve weeks of listing.
photoDirection: Pair on Burrard Inlet with mountains behind. Archive-feel treatment to signal the listing is closed.

title: 2018 Sykes Single Scull
highlights: Suits a lightweight or junior sculler
Rigged and ready — nothing to buy on day one
Freight to the east coast can be arranged
description: Club single used by our lightweight women's group. The weight band is genuinely 62–76 kg; a heavier sculler will sit the boat too deep and hate it, so please check before travelling. Hull is sound with normal club scratching. Wing rigger is straight, tracks are good, and it comes rigged with shoes, bow ball and a cover. We can put it on a freight trailer heading east if that helps.
photoDirection: Single on the Swan River with the Perth skyline low behind, hard Australian afternoon light. Detail of the aluminium wing rigger and the club decal.

title: New Croker S4 Sculls — Pair
highlights: Adjustable length 284–290 cm
Choice of blade profile at order
In stock, ships worldwide
description: New pair of Croker S4 sculls, adjustable 284–290 cm, supplied with your choice of blade profile and your club's paint scheme if you send artwork. Croker shafts are the default across most of Australia and New Zealand for good reason — they are stiff, consistent between pairs, and the handles wear well. Grips fitted as standard; a second set of grips is included.
photoDirection: Blades laid on a boathouse floor, painted in club colours, overhead flat-lay. Close-up of the handle and collar. Blades feathering at the finish, spray caught in the light.

title: Used Concept2 Skinny Blade Sculls — Pair
highlights: A cheap, honest first pair of sculls
Shafts straight, blades chipped
Collars and grips included
description: Club sculls retired from our fleet. Shafts are straight and stiff with no cracks; the blade edges are chipped in several places from dock contact, which affects looks more than performance for a training pair. Grips are worn but usable and we will include a spare set. Set at 286 cm. Perfectly good for someone learning or wanting a knockabout spare pair.
photoDirection: Pair of well-used blades leaning against a weathered boathouse wall, Minnesota winter light. Honest close-up of the chipped blade edges.

title: Used Brača Sweep Oars — Set of Eight
highlights: Complete matched set of eight
One consistent batch — same stiffness throughout
Repainted in plain white, ready for your colours
description: A full matched set of eight sweep oars from a single production batch, which matters: mixed-batch sets never feel the same across a crew. Set at 376 cm with the standard Braca 31 blade. Used for six seasons, then stripped and repainted plain white when we changed suppliers. Two shafts have minor cosmetic repairs at the collar; all eight are straight and stiff.
photoDirection: Eight blades stacked in a rack, plain white, geometric repetition. Detail of a collar and the repainted shaft. A crew's blades all locked in at the catch.

title: New Concept2 Fat2 Sweep Oars — Set of Four
highlights: Set of four, matched stiffness
Adjustable length, standard or soft shaft
Custom blade paint at no extra cost
description: New set of four Fat2 sweep oars, matched for stiffness and supplied adjustable. Choose standard or soft shafts at order — soft suits lighter or junior crews and most people order the wrong one, so ask if you are unsure. Custom blade paint in your club colours is included in the price. Ships from Vermont; two-week turnaround on painted sets.
photoDirection: Four fresh blades in a rack, paint crisp, studio-clean lighting. Detail of the Fat2 blade face. Wide shot of a four with blades buried at the catch.

title: Used Dreher Sculling Oars — Pair
highlights: Adjustable-length shafts
Ergonomic wooden handles — kinder on the hands
One careful owner
description: My training sculls for eight years, bought new and used only by me. Adjustable shafts currently set to 285 cm. The wooden handles are the reason I bought them — they are noticeably kinder on the hands than rubber grips over a long steady-state row, and they have worn evenly. Blades have the usual light chipping. Selling with the boat they came with is not an option; the boat is staying.
photoDirection: Pair of sculls across a dock in low autumn light, New England river behind. Warm close-up of the wooden handles showing even wear.

title: Used Four-Boat Club Trailer
highlights: Carries four eights or a mixed load of smaller boats
Aluminium frame — no rust
Lights, brakes and bearings serviced March 2026
description: Our regatta trailer for eleven years. Aluminium frame so there is no rust anywhere, which is the thing that kills steel trailers on the coast. Carries four eights, or a mixed load — we have run two eights, a quad and two singles on it many times. Full service in March 2026: new bearings, new lights, brakes checked. Straps and eight sets of padded cradles included. California registration is current.
photoDirection: Loaded trailer at a regatta site at dawn, boats strapped and covered, mist on the course. Detail of the cradles and the tie-down system. Hitch and lighting board close-up.

title: Used Eight-Shell Regatta Trailer
highlights: Eight-shell capacity with adjustable racking
TÜV valid to 2028
Integrated oar box for 40 blades
description: Eight-boat regatta trailer with adjustable racking, so it will take eights, fours and singles in any sensible combination. Integrated lockable oar box holds forty blades, which removes the single most annoying part of running a regatta trip. TÜV valid until 2028. Galvanised steel frame, kept under cover between trips, no corrosion. Selling because we have merged fleets with a neighbouring club and now need a twelve.
photoDirection: Trailer on the road with a full load, autobahn light. Detail of the adjustable racking arms and the oar box interior packed with blades.

title: Used Filippi Wing Rigger Set — Single
highlights: Fits current-generation Filippi singles
Complete with gates, pins and spacers
Straight — checked on a rigging jig
description: Spare wing rigger from my Filippi F1, sold because I have gone back to the boat's original set. Fits current-generation Filippi singles; check your hull mounting points before buying if yours is pre-2015. Complete with both gates, pins, and a full bag of spacers. Checked straight on a club rigging jig last month. Light scratching on the carbon, nothing structural.
photoDirection: Wing rigger on a workshop bench, raking light picking out the carbon weave. Detail of the gate and pin assembly. The rigger sitting on a jig.

title: 2023 Empacher Lightweight Single
highlights: Three seasons old, effectively as new
Lightweight layup for scullers 58–70 kg
Original invoice and build sheet included
description: Bought new in 2023 for the lightweight category and used for three seasons of domestic racing. Freshwater only, indoor storage, covered, and never trailered further than Denmark. There is one small scuff on the stern deck and that is genuinely the only mark on it. Original invoice and Empacher build sheet included, which makes resale easier for you later. Selling because I have moved up a weight class.
photoDirection: Single on a Copenhagen canal at blue hour, warm window light on the banks. Studio-clean detail of the near-perfect deck. The build sheet photographed on a table.
